tagline: Storage for anything, at any scale
what: Simple Storage Service: put files ("objects") into buckets and fetch them back over HTTPS, from anywhere.
facts: S3 launched on 14 March 2006 (Pi Day), making it one of the very first AWS services.
It is designed for 99.999999999% (eleven nines) durability, and a single object can be up to 5 TB.
inAmacide: Every drawing you submit goes straight from your phone into an S3 bucket through a presigned URL.
promptHint: buckets, storing and losing things, overflowing storage

examples.draw: A bucket overflowing with cat photos
examples.learn: What does Amazon S3 store, and how do you get things back out?
examples.wit: The weirdest thing someone has stored in an S3 bucket

tagline: Run code without thinking about servers
what: Upload a function and Lambda runs it whenever something happens: an HTTP request, a file upload, a message. You pay only while it runs.
facts: Lambda was announced in 2014 and kicked off the whole "serverless" movement.
A single invocation can run for up to 15 minutes, and it is billed per millisecond.
inAmacide: Every button you press in this game (join, submit, start) is handled by a Lambda function.
promptHint: functions, cold starts, running fast, events

examples.draw: A tiny function sprinting to finish before its timeout
examples.learn: What does AWS Lambda let you avoid managing?
examples.wit: What a Lambda function does between invocations

tagline: A database that stays fast at any size
what: A fully managed NoSQL key-value database: single-digit millisecond reads and writes, whether you have ten items or ten billion.
facts: DynamoDB launched in 2012, built on lessons from Amazon's 2007 "Dynamo" paper about the shopping cart.
There are no servers to manage: tables scale up and down automatically with on-demand capacity.
inAmacide: Rooms, players, answers and scores all live in a single DynamoDB table (single-table design).
promptHint: tables, keys, speed, organising huge amounts of things

examples.draw: A robot librarian sorting a billion books at lightning speed
examples.learn: When would you pick DynamoDB over a traditional SQL database?
examples.wit: A terrible name for a partition key

what: A fully managed way to use foundation models from several AI companies (including Anthropic's Claude) through a single API, with guardrails and knowledge bases built in.
facts: Bedrock became generally available in September 2023.
Your data sent to Bedrock is not used to train the underlying models.
inAmacide: Bedrock is the AI you're playing against: it writes every prompt and judges every answer.
promptHint: AI, robots, models, the AI judge itself

examples.draw: A caveman chatting with an AI on a stone tablet
examples.learn: What does Amazon Bedrock give you access to?
examples.wit: What the AI really thinks of humans

what: Text-to-speech as a service: send text (or SSML for pauses and emphasis) and get back natural-sounding audio in dozens of voices and languages.
facts: Polly launched at re:Invent 2016.
Its neural voices use deep learning to sound far more natural than older text-to-speech.
inAmacide: The game-show host voice that reads out the winners and roasts is generated by Polly.

examples.draw: A parrot reading the evening news
examples.learn: What does Amazon Polly turn text into?
examples.wit: The worst thing to make a text-to-speech voice say

what: Chain services together into a visual workflow: each step runs, retries on failure and hands its output to the next, all defined in Amazon States Language.
facts: Step Functions launched at re:Invent 2016.
Standard workflows can run for up to a year, with built-in retries and error handling.
inAmacide: Judging each round is a Step Functions workflow: Judge → Host voice → Save results.

examples.draw: A robot stuck in an infinite loop on a flowchart
examples.learn: What is AWS Step Functions for when you have several steps?
examples.wit: A step that should never be in any workflow

what: A content delivery network: copies of your website are cached at hundreds of edge locations worldwide, so pages load fast wherever people are.
facts: CloudFront launched in 2008.
Edge caching means most requests never reach your origin server at all.
inAmacide: CloudFront serves this game to your phone over HTTPS, so it loads fast from the QR code.
promptHint: delivery, speed, the whole world visiting at once

examples.draw: A delivery pigeon with a jetpack
examples.learn: How does Amazon CloudFront make a website load faster?
examples.wit: The worst thing to cache at the edge

what: Elastic Compute Cloud: rent virtual machines by the second, from tiny to enormous, with GPUs and custom chips like AWS Graviton.
facts: EC2 launched in 2006, the same year as S3.
There are hundreds of instance types, each tuned for a different kind of workload.
inAmacide: We don't use EC2 at all! Amacide is fully serverless, so there's no server to run or pay for when idle.
promptHint: servers, instances, forgetting to turn things off, big bills

examples.draw: A server rack on a beach holiday
examples.learn: What does Amazon EC2 give you, and how is it billed?
examples.wit: A name for an instance type that doesn't exist yet

what: Computer vision as an API: detect objects, text and faces in images and video, and flag unsafe content with moderation labels.
facts: Rekognition launched at re:Invent 2016, alongside Polly.
Its content moderation labels can flag unsafe images automatically.
inAmacide: Rekognition's moderation can check drawings before they appear on the big screen (a planned stretch goal).
promptHint: cameras, recognising things, labels, getting it wrong

examples.draw: A robot eye judging a fashion show
examples.learn: What can Amazon Rekognition find in an image?
examples.wit: Something an image AI should never label

what: Managed GraphQL and Pub/Sub APIs. AppSync Events adds serverless WebSockets: publish to a channel and every subscriber gets it instantly.
facts: AppSync became generally available in 2018.
AppSync Events, launched in 2024, gives you WebSocket channels without managing any connections yourself.
inAmacide: AppSync Events pushes live updates like "round started" and "results ready" to every phone.
promptHint: real-time messages, broadcasting, everyone getting a notification at once

examples.draw: Two phones sending each other messages at lightning speed
examples.learn: What does AWS AppSync Events let a server push to clients?
examples.wit: The worst message to broadcast to every phone at once

what: A storefront to allow access to non-AWS services alongside AWS ones
facts: AWS Marketplace was launched in 2012
There are 42,240 products and services on AWS marketplace
inAmacide: We don't use any marketplace products.
